validation.notes: Node 24 runs .prale-eval/regression.mjs, which links the submitted production modules through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (real DefaultResourceLoader, SettingsManager and resolveProjectTrusted; only settings storage, package-manager, extension-loader, trust-store and prompt-UI boundaries faked). It asserts the restored end-to-end boundary: (1) loadProjectTrustExtensions() demotes an already-trusted manager, so the bootstrap pass reads global configuration only, performs no project settings storage IO and loads just the cli+global extension set; (2) an explicit trustOverride=false wins without prompting or persisting even when a UI and a permissive default/stored decision are available, explicit true wins over a stored false and a 'never' default, persisted decisions still apply without prompting, and an unknown state without UI stays untrusted; (3) a later trusted reload admits the project extension on top of the reused pre-trust runtime while keeping cli+global resources, merging nested settings recursively (project compaction.reserveTokens=4096 overrides, global keepRecentTokens=2000 inherited) and leaving the global scope untouched; (4) SettingsManager alone never reads project storage before consent (storage-scope spies) and only reports a corrupt project settings parse error after trust is granted. Mutation check run locally and reverted: restoring any single faulty baseline (settings-manager.ts 'if (false)', resource-loader.ts setProjectTrusted(true), project-trust.ts 'if (options.trustOverride)') makes the script fail with an uncaught AssertionError (exit 1), never an import error, crash or timeout. Limitation: the repo's vitest suite and tsc are unavailable because node_modules is absent and dependencies must not be installed, so this script is the validation evidence.

claims.claim: The bootstrap pass loadProjectTrustExtensions() forced this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(true), so an already-trusted manager kept its project settings and the pre-trust extension set leaked project resources; it now forces false.

SettingsManager.loadFromStorage() ignored the projectTrusted argument (guard reduced to 'if (false)'), parsing and merging the project settings file while untrusted; the guard is restored to 'if (scope === "project" && !projectTrusted)' and runs before any storage access.

resolveProjectTrusted() used a truthiness test on trustOverride, discarding an explicit false and falling through to extension hook/store/default/prompt; it now tests 'trustOverride !== undefined' so explicit true and false both win without prompting.
